settings.heading: The difference vs. a piston compressor.
settings.lead: Piston (reciprocating) compressors are the value choice for intermittent use. Once air is running for hours at a time, a rotary screw is the tool for the job.

settings.title: Continuous duty
settings.text: A rotary screw runs 100% of the time without overheating. A piston unit is designed to build pressure and rest; push it and it wears fast.

settings.title: More air per horsepower
settings.text: Screw compressors deliver more usable CFM for the same motor size, and hold pressure steady instead of cycling up and down.

settings.title: Clean, dry air built in
settings.text: Compressing air makes water. The integrated refrigerated dryer removes it before it reaches your lines, protecting finishes, tools and fittings from rust.

settings.title: Quieter, and lower running cost
settings.text: Enclosed and vibration-isolated, it's quieter than an open piston pump, and the cost per CFM over its life is lower.

settings.heading: Power, space and setup to plan for.
settings.lead: A machine this size needs a few things in place. Check these before ordering, and involve a licensed electrician and a compressed-air installer for the hookup.

settings.title: Three-phase power
settings.text: A 20 HP motor needs 3-phase service and a correctly sized breaker and feeder. Confirm your building's supply with an electrician.

settings.title: Placement and ventilation
settings.text: A dry, level, ventilated area with clearance around the enclosure for cooling airflow. Keep it out of freezing temperatures.

settings.title: Air distribution
settings.text: Hard-piped drops sloped to drip legs, air taken off the top of the line, isolation valves per bay. The 500 L tank buffers demand across the shop.

settings.title: Condensate handling
settings.text: The dryer and tank produce condensate. Plan a drain line and, where required, an oil-water separator to meet local disposal rules.

settings.question: What is a rotary screw air compressor?
settings.answer: A rotary screw compressor uses two interlocking helical rotors to compress air in a continuous flow, instead of a piston pumping in strokes. That lets it run 100% of the time without overheating, hold pressure steady and deliver more air per horsepower, which is why it's the standard for shops that use air for hours at a stretch.

settings.question: What size air compressor does a busy auto or body shop need?
settings.answer: Add up the CFM at 90 psi of every air tool you'll run at the same time, then add about 30% headroom. Multi-bay shops running sanders, impacts and spray guns all day are what this 20 HP unit is built to supply, with the 500 L tank buffering peaks.

settings.question: Does this compressor need three-phase power?
settings.answer: Yes. A 20 HP motor requires 3-phase electrical service with a properly sized breaker and feeder. Most commercial and industrial buildings have it; confirm your supply with a licensed electrician before ordering.

settings.question: Do I need to buy a separate air dryer?
settings.answer: No. A refrigerated air dryer is built into this package, so you get clean, dry air out of the box, which matters for spray finishing, plasma cutting and the life of your air tools. Additional point-of-use filtration can be added for specific processes.

settings.question: Is this worth it for a home garage?
settings.answer: For a serious home shop (restoration, fabrication, a car collection), yes: it's quiet, gives you clean dry air with no bolt-on dryer, runs any tool without waiting, and it's the last compressor you'll buy. It does need 3-phase power or a phase converter. For occasional tyre-and-nailer use it's more than you need; send us your setup and we'll be straight with you.

settings.question: How is it delivered and installed?
settings.answer: It ships free on a pallet anywhere in Canada, or you can pick it up in Richmond, Vancouver or Calgary. Position it with a pallet jack or forklift onto a level pad. Hookup needs a licensed electrician for the 3-phase connection and a compressed-air installer for piping and drains.

settings.question: Is financing available?
settings.answer: Yes, TOOSA offers monthly payment plans through RBC on the compressor, the same as our tool storage. Ask us for terms, or start your order and choose the financing option at checkout.

settings.question: CFM vs. PSI, what should I size against?
settings.answer: PSI is pressure; almost any compressor makes enough. CFM (airflow) at working pressure is what runs your tools continuously, so size against the combined CFM of everything running at once.
